discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 100726
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
226 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Sunshine today with highs into the low-mid 60s. 

- A low pressure system moves through Wednesday afternoon into 
  Wednesday night with a period of rain.

- Lake effect showers impact areas mainly west of US-31 in nw IN
  and far sw MI Thursday through Friday night. Snow may mix in 
  by late Thursday night into Friday morning. 

- Below normal temperatures Thursday through this weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 226 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

Another pleasant and mild day today despite a weak, washed out, 
frontal passage as another shortwave bypasses well north through the 
northern and eastern Great Lakes. This flattened, high latitude, 
flow then gives way to a full-latitude longwave trough over the 
Eastern CONUS by the second half of this week. This transition will 
drive a compact shortwave southeast through the area Wednesday 
afternoon-evening. The associated frontal wave and pacific moisture 
origins will bring chances (50-80%) for a period of rain during this 
time, with a few heavier convective elements possible south of US-30 
near the sfc low track and steeper mid level lapse rates. 

Colder air wraps in behind this low Thursday into Friday as several 
more shortwave impulses drop through the region in deep northerly 
flow. A secondary trough and steepening lapse rates with the cold 
pool will keep chances for scattered rain showers in the forecast 
area-wide into Thursday. This chilly northerly flow (850 mb temps 
fall to near -5C) brings about a full transition to lake effect rain 
otherwise Thursday through Friday night. Favorable long lake 
fetch/convergence and thermal parameters will allow for more 
organized lake effect banding to settle into our northerly flow lake 
belts at times, mainly west of US-31 in far nw IN (especially 
LaPorte/Starke counties Thursday night-Friday). Wet-bulb zero 
heights may collapse to less than 1 kft later Thursday night into 
Friday morning just inland from the lake. The NBM and ensemble 
guidance hint at the potential for slushy snow accums here (mainly 
LaPorte/Starke Ct). Confidence is low given lingering uncertainties 
regarding low level flow trajectories, warm lake and marginally cold 
nature to the incoming air mass. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1223 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

VFR conditions expected through the TAF period. Winds veering
from southwesterly to more westerly after 10z Tue and remain 
light, less than 10 knots.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 100537

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1137 PM CST Mon Nov 09 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected Tuesday through Tuesday night.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...

   A progressive and amplifying polar branch of westerlies is forecast
   over the northern CONUS Tuesday and Tuesday night. Within that air
   stream, a short-wave trough will move through the Northeast, while
   an upstream system intensifies over the northern Plains and Upper
   Midwest. Meanwhile, a lower-latitude system over TX is expected to
   de-amplify while advancing into the lower MS Valley. At the surface,
   a lee cyclone and attending trough initially over the High Plains
   will shift east through the northern and central Plains into the
   Midwest, in tandem with the previously mentioned upper-air system.
   Increasing southerly flow ahead of that frontal system will support
   the poleward advance of a partially modified continental-polar air
   mass from the southern Plains into the Ozarks.

   Isolated thunderstorms appear possible along the middle TX Coast
   Tuesday morning, and from the middle TX Coast into southern LA
   Tuesday night, within a zone of low-level warm advection and weak
   instability preceding the midlevel wave. Along the Pacific Northwest
   Coast, moist onshore flow coupled with a slight steepening of
   midlevel lapse rates will yield weak instability and the potential
   for isolated thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Over
   south FL, slight cooling aloft will combine with a moist PBL to
   yield MUCAPE of around 1000 J/kg by afternoon when isolated
   thunderstorms appear possible.
     
   Elsewhere, isolated lightning strikes appear possible over northern
   or central TX, northern New England, and perhaps the eastern Dakotas
   Tuesday afternoon into evening. Lightning duration and coverage in
   those areas appear too limited to warrant general thunderstorm/10%
   probability contours.

   ..Mead.. 11/10/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts will be possible on Wednesday across parts of the lower Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys.
spc.text:
SPC AC 100649

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1249 AM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE LOWER OHIO AND WESTERN TENNESSEE VALLEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts will be possible on
   Wednesday across parts of the lower Ohio and western Tennessee
   Valleys.

   ...Lower Ohio and Western Tennessee Valleys...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will dig southeastward into the mid
   Mississippi Valley on Wednesday. Ahead of the trough, moisture
   advection will take place with surface dewpoints reaching the mid
   50s F over parts of the lower Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys by
   afternoon. Surface heating will result in weak destabilization along
   and near a moist axis. Near this axis, large-scale ascent associated
   with the trough will aid convective development in the late
   afternoon and early evening. Scattered storms appear likely to
   develop near the confluence of the Mississippi and Ohio Rivers
   and spread eastward across southern Indiana, western Kentucky and
   northern Tennessee during the early evening. RRFS forecast soundings
   across western Kentucky at 00Z have MLCAPE near 500 J/kg with 0-6 km
   shear around 50 knots. This may be sufficient for a marginal severe
   threat with a few severe wind gusts possible. However, lapse rates
   are forecast to be poor which will be a limiting factor, helping to
   keep any severe threat localized.

   ..Broyles.. 11/10/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

   Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Thursday and
   Thursday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level trough will move across the eastern U.S. on Thursday,
   as a cold front advances eastward through the Atlantic coastal
   states. During the day, thunderstorms will be possible along and
   ahead of the front from the Mid-Atlantic southward into far eastern
   North Carolina. Instability is expected to be too weak for a severe
   threat. Elsewhere across the continental U.S., no severe threat is
   forecast Thursday and Thursday night.

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
